'''Kilmarnock Football Club''' is a Scottish professional [[Association football|football]] team based in the town of [[Kilmarnock]] in [[East Ayrshire]], that currently plays in the {{Scottish football updater|Kilmarno}}. The club has achieved several honours since its formation in 1869,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.kilmarnockfc.co.uk/|title=Official Website of Kilmarnock FC|website=Kilmarnockfc.co.uk|access-date=22 June 2011|archive-date=17 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210217184906/http://www.kilmarnockfc.co.uk/|url-status=live}}</ref> most recently the [[2011–12 Scottish League Cup]] after a [[2012 Scottish League Cup final|1–0 win]] over [[Celtic F.C.|Celtic]] at [[Hampden Park]]<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/17330246|title=Celtic 0–1 Kilmarnock|publisher=BBC Sport|date=18 March 2012|access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=6 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160106020401/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/football/17330246|url-status=live}}</ref> and the [[Scottish Championship]] title in 2022. The club nickname, ''Killie'', is the Scottish term for the town of Kilmarnock.

The club have qualified for European competitions on nine occasions, their best performance coming in the [[1966–67 Inter-Cities Fairs Cup|1966–67 Fairs Cup]] when they progressed to the semi-finals, eventually being eliminated by [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]]. The club is also one of only a few Scottish clubs to have played in three European competitions ([[UEFA Champions League|European Cup]], [[UEFA Cup Winners' Cup|Cup Winners' Cup]] and the [[UEFA Europa League|UEFA Cup]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.killiefc.com/Web%20Pages/EuroKillie.htm|title=Killie in Europe!!|website=Killiefc.com|access-date=30 July 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131121044922/http://www.killiefc.com/Web%20Pages/EuroKillie.htm|archive-date=21 November 2013|url-status=dead}}</ref> Additionally, the club have played in the [[International Soccer League]] four times – [[1960 International Soccer League|1960]], [[1961 International Soccer League|1961]], [[1963 International Soccer League|1963]] and [[1965 International Soccer League|1965]], as well as competing in the [[1995 Korea Cup]].<ref name="Kilmarnock Football Club Ltd">{{cite book |last1=Cairns, Livingston |first1=Richard, John |title=Kilmarnock Football Club: 150 Years In the Making |date=2019 |publisher=Kilmarnock Football Club Ltd. |page=140}}</ref> Their most recent appearance in European competition football was during the [[2024–25 UEFA Europa League]] and [[2024–25 UEFA Conference League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The official website for European football |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaeuropaleague/clubs/62178--kilmarnock/ |website=[[UEFA]] |access-date=30 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The official website for European football |url=https://www.uefa.com/uefaconferenceleague/clubs/62178--kilmarnock/ |website=[[UEFA]] |access-date=30 August 2024 |language=en}}</ref>

Kilmarnock Football Club is currently the oldest football club in the [[Scottish Premiership]], and also the second-oldest professional club in Scotland.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.scotsman.com/news/who-are-scotland-s-oldest-professional-football-clubs-1-4098282|title=Who are Scotland's oldest professional football clubs|website=Scotsman.com|access-date=21 May 2017|archive-date=1 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170601094134/http://www.scotsman.com/news/who-are-scotland-s-oldest-professional-football-clubs-1-4098282|url-status=live}}</ref> Home matches are played at [[Rugby Park]], a 15,003 capacity [[all-seater stadium]] situated in the town itself. Kilmarnock took part in the first-ever official match in the [[Scottish Cup]] against the now-defunct [[Renton F.C.|Renton]] in 1873. With a long-standing football rivalry with fellow [[Ayrshire]] side [[Ayr United F.C.|Ayr United]], both teams play frequently in the [[Ayrshire derby]], first meeting in September 1910."}}
